title: intent set <ST> completed records a value that is not a date, and a completion date on a thread that is not closed
body:
Raised by vc on 2026-09-22, found while re-driving row C6 of the Conflab and Baize holds triage (`intent/history/20260921-triage-conflab-baize-holds.md`). That row names `intent set <ST> completed <date>` as the way to write Conflab's missing completion dates, and says by source read that the verb validates nothing, which had not been driven.

**What was seen.** On the installed pair at c3514e151 (`intent 3.2.0 (c3514e151...)`), in a scratch project under an isolated HOME, every verb run in-process:

- `intent set ST0002 completed not-a-date` prints `ok: intent:///threads/ST0002 completed written` at rc 0, and `intent st show ST0002` then reads `completed: not-a-date`.
- `intent set ST0003 completed 2026-03-03`, on a thread in Triage, prints the same `ok:` at rc 0, and `intent st show ST0003` reads `status: Triage` beside `completed: 2026-03-03`.

**What was expected.** The field refuses through `set` what it refuses through `st done`. On the move from WIP to Completed, `intent st done ST0004 --date not-a-date` is refused at rc 1 ("`completed` was given `not-a-date`, which this field cannot record: this field records ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`, with no time component"). The status writer also refuses a date on any move that closes nothing. Its own comment gives the reason both refusals are owed at every door: "A malformed date reaching canon is unrecoverable by inspection: the field has no time component, so `2026-02-30` reads as data rather than as an error for as long as it sits there" (`native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/facade.rs:11822-11851`).

**Where.** `Facade::set` (`facade.rs:14824`) writes an addressed field generically and re-parses the result by the model's type. A thread's `completed` is a string in the model, so the re-parse accepts any string, and nothing on this path reads the thread's status. The date is validated by exactly one of the two doors that write the field.
